one_liner: Step-by-step AVX-512 DGEMM tutorial whose final kernel roughly matches single-threaded Intel MKL on large square matrices.
what_it_does: A teaching repo of 19 column-major DGEMM kernels, from a naive triple loop to a packed, cache-blocked AVX-512 inline-assembly kernel (18 serial, 19 OpenMP). Each kernel is a C function mydgemm_cpu_vN(M,N,K,alpha,A,LDA,B,LDB,beta,C,LDC) covering only the column-major, no-transpose case; there is no BLAS-compatible API.
how_it_is_fast: Goto/BLIS-style blocking (M=192, K=384, N=8640 blocks) with packing of A and B into 4096-byte-aligned buffers, and a 24x8 register-blocked micro-kernel in AVX-512 inline asm (vbroadcastsd + vfmadd231pd on zmm registers). It adds software prefetching (prefetcht0) on A, B and C, a tuned C-scaling routine, and 'discontinuous' packing of B meant to help the L2 hardware prefetcher. Kernel 19 parallelises over M with a shared packed-B buffer and OpenMP barriers.
when_to_use: Learning or teaching how a BLIS/Goto-style DGEMM is built on AVX-512, one optimisation at a time
Vendoring a small, readable FP64 GEMM micro-kernel into GPL-compatible code on Skylake-X/Cascade Lake-class CPUs
Large square column-major FP64 GEMM (about n >= 1600), where kernel 18 was a few percent ahead of single-threaded MKL on a Xeon W-2255
As a starting point for your own AVX-512 kernel tuning experiments
when_not_to_use: Small and mid-size matrices: in the repo's own plot kernel 18 trails MKL by roughly 10-20% for n=200..1500
Any production BLAS need: only NN column-major DGEMM, no transposes, no other precisions or routines; use MKL, OpenBLAS or BLIS
CPUs without AVX-512F (all AMD before Zen 4, most Intel client chips), or non-x86
Multi-threaded claims: the harness links mkl_sequential and run.sh sets MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, so the parallel kernel 19 was never compared to threaded MKL

integration.dependencies: OpenMP (kernel 19); Intel MKL only for the test harness and correctness reference
integration.min_toolchain: GCC with AT&T inline asm and -march=skylake-avx512 (tested with GCC 7.3.0); C11 aligned_alloc
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each call allocates its own packing buffers, kernel 19 spawns its own OpenMP team
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same argument order as column-major cblas_dgemm NN, but 32-bit int dims, no layout/transpose flags, separate function per kernel

gotchas: If alpha==0 or K==0 the function returns without applying beta to C, unlike BLAS semantics (C = beta*C)
Correctness check in the harness uses an absolute tolerance of 1e-2, which is loose
Timing is 3 repetitions via gettimeofday with no warm-up; MKL's 7 GFLOPS at n=100 in the plot looks like a first-call artifact
The Makefile builds everything at -O0; the hot path is inline asm so this matters less, but the C driver/packing code is unoptimised
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over llamafile tinyBLAS or TCL when you want FP64 GEMM on AVX-512 and readable, staged code to learn from; tinyBLAS targets FP16/BF16/quantised LLM matmuls and TCL targets tensor contractions on top of a BLAS.
verified_claims_summary: On one Intel Xeon W-2255 core (GCC 7.3.0, -march=skylake-avx512, oneMKL 2021.1 beta sequential), the repo's plot shows kernel 18 at about 33-115 GFLOPS across square n=100..3000, behind MKL from n=200 to 1500 and about 2-8% ahead from n=1600 to 3000 (about 115 vs 110 GFLOPS at n=3000, read from the plot). No measurement of the parallel kernel 19 against MKL was found.
status_note: Abandoned since February 2022 and tutorial code, but GPL-3.0 and small (one ~670-line header per kernel), so it can be vendored by GPL projects; last tested compiler GCC 7.3.0.
